'''Rui António Loja Fernandes''' (July 20, 1965, [[Coimbra]]) is a [[Portugal|Portuguese]] mathematician working in the [[United States|USA]].

== Education and career ==
Fernandes obtained a bachelor's degree in Physics Engineering at [[Instituto Superior Técnico]] ([[Lisbon]], Portugal) in 1988. He then moved to the USA and earned a master's degree in Mathematics in 1991 and a PhD in Mathematics in 1994 from the [[University of Minnesota]]. His PhD thesis was entitled "''Completely Integrable bi-Hamiltonian Systems"'' and has been written under the supervision of [[Peter J. Olver]].<ref name=":0">{{mathgenealogy|id=2073}}</ref> 

In 1994 he returned to [[Instituto Superior Técnico]], where he worked first as Assistant Professor (1994-2002), and then as Associated Professor (2003-2007) and Full Professor (2007-2012).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rui Loja Fernandes{{!}} DMIST|url=https://www.math.tecnico.ulisboa.pt/~rfern/index.php|access-date=2021-03-27|website=www.math.tecnico.ulisboa.pt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=CAMGSD — Members|url=https://camgsd.tecnico.ulisboa.pt/membros/|access-date=2021-03-27|website=camgsd.tecnico.ulisboa.pt|language=en}}</ref>

In 2012 he moved back to the USA and since then he is the Lois M. Lackner Professor of Mathematics at [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rui Loja Fernandes|url=http://www.math.illinois.edu/~ruiloja/|accessdate=May 13, 2017|publisher=illinois.edu}}</ref> In 2016, he became a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to the study of Poisson geometry and Lie algebroids, and for service to the mathematical community."<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieves 2017-08-09.</ref>

== Research ==
Fernandes research focusses on [[differential geometry]], more precisely on [[Poisson manifold|Poisson]] and [[Symplectic geometry|symplectic]] geometry. Among his most well-known results are a solution to the long-standing problem of describing the obstructions to the integrability of [[Lie algebroid|Lie algebroids]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Fernandes|first2=Rui|date=2003-03-01|title=Integrability of Lie brackets|url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2003/157-2/p06|journal=Annals of Mathematics|language=en|volume=157|issue=2|pages=575–620|doi=10.4007/annals.2003.157.575|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0105033}}</ref> and a new geometric proof of Conn's linearization theorem,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Fernandes|first2=Rui Loja|date=2011-03-01|title=A geometric approach to Conn's linearization theorem|url=http://annals.math.princeton.edu/2011/173-2/p14|journal=Annals of Mathematics|language=en|volume=173|issue=2|pages=1121–1139|doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.2.14|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=0812.3060}}</ref> both written in collaboration with [[Marius Crainic]].

He is the author of more than 40 research papers in peer-reviewed journals<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rui Loja Fernandes|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=E7vFQykAAAAJ&hl=en|access-date=2021-03-27|website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> and has supervised 6 PhD students as of 2021.<ref name=":0" />
